\mathrm{\Phi }( \theta ,z )=( 2 \cos \theta ,2 \sin \theta ,z ),\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le z\le 5 [Step 1.] Compute the tangent and normal vectors.
The tangent vectors are the partial derivatives: {\mathbf{T} }_{\theta }=\frac{\partial \mathrm{\Phi }}{\partial \theta }=\frac{\partial }{\partial \theta }( 2 \cos \theta ,2 \sin \theta ,z )= \left\lt -2 \sin \theta ,2 \cos \theta ,0 \right> {\mathbf{T} }_z =\frac{\partial }{\partial z}( 2 \cos \theta ,2 \sin \theta ,z )= \left\lt 0,0,1 \right> The normal vector is their cross product: \mathbf{n} ( \theta ,z )={\mathbf{T} }_{\theta }\times {\mathbf{T} }_z = \left|\begin{array}{ccc}\mathbf{i} \amp \mathbf{j} \amp \mathbf{k} \\ -2 \sin \theta \amp 2 \cos \theta \amp 0\\ 0\amp 0\amp 1\end{array}\right|= ( 2 \cos \theta ) \mathbf{i} +( 2 \sin \theta ) \mathbf{j}= \left\lt 2 \cos \theta ,2 \sin \theta ,0 \right> The length of the normal vector is thus \| \mathbf{n} ( \theta ,z )\|=\sqrt{{( 2 \cos \theta )}^2+{( 2 \sin \theta )}^2+0}=\sqrt{4\left(\cos^2 \theta +\sin^2 \theta \right)}=\sqrt{4}=2 [Step 2.] Calculate the surface integral.
The surface integral equals the following double integral: \iint_S f( x,y,z ) \,dS =\iint_{\mathcal{D}} f\left(\mathrm{\Phi }( \theta ,z )\right)\| \mathbf{n} \| \,d\theta \,dz=\int_0^{2\pi } \int_0^{5} e^{-z}\cdot 2 \,d\theta \,dz =\left(\int_0^{2\pi } 2 \,d\theta \right)\left(\int_0^{5} e^{-z} \,dz\right)= 4\pi \cdot \left(- {e^{-z}} \right)\bigg|_0^{5}=4\pi \left(1- e^{-5}\right)
